Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Pulp and Paper Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Report LBNL-2268E, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, October 2009. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue; nearly every number is reprinted from other sources (named in each note). Main file: Appendix Table E.1 best-available-technology energy use (Jacobs and IPST 2006 via NCASI 2009) for 11 pulping routes, 15 paper grades and market pulp, loaded as final electricity, steam and direct fuel per tonne (converted from per-short-ton with explicit formulas; zero direct fuel not loaded); Table 4.2 boiler efficiencies by fuel (recovery, gas, wood/bark, coal, residual and distillate oil); recovery boiler 65% (Sect. 3.3) and Tomlinson 65-70% (Ch.18); market pulp drying 4.2 MMBtu/t steam; CHP availability (combined cycle 77-85%, boiler/steam turbine 90-95%), SP Newsprint 92 MW gas-turbine CHP ($75 million), micro back-pressure turbine ($600/kWe, $0.011/kWh), STIG sizes; chip conveyors (18.2 vs 1 kWh/ton); live-steam log thawing (0.5 MMBtu/ADT); TMP heat recovery (capex, steam flow); recycled pulp capacity capex; shoe press, gap former vs Fourdrinier, closed hood, paper machine heat recovery and CondeBelt costs; black liquor gasifier descriptions/status; microwave log treatment capex. Flows: TMP refiner heat recovery 1.1-1.9 t clean steam per t pulp. _measures.csv: quantified measures of Chapters 6-18 with saving, cost and payback as printed (cross-cutting chapters selectively). _other-values.csv: Table 4.1/4.2 sector totals, mixed-carrier route totals (p.27), Table 4.3 CO2 factors, sector GHG, yields. Not loaded: water measures (Ch.19), Appendix E.2/E.3 lists (no numbers), figures read only from charts (Figs 4.1-4.6, 8.1), case-study dollar savings without energy.

(1) Table E.1 is per short ton and BAT, reprinted from Jacobs and IPST (2006); pulping rows cover whole routes (kraft includes bleaching, recovery and lime kiln), papermaking rows whole machines. (2) No price year for any cost; costs from Martin et al. (2000) per ton are read as per annual ton of capacity (not stated). SP Newsprint $75 million is a 1999-2000 project. (3) Heating-value basis never stated. (4) Table 4.1/4.2 column headers are garbled in text extraction; column order (black liquor, natural gas, wood and bark, coal, net electricity, residual oil, distillate, other) confirmed by row sums and the text (coal 11% of inputs).
